newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta City Council approves new Hawks arena deal.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta City Council approves new Hawks arena deal.

text.p: The Atlanta City Council unanimously approved a revised agreement for the Hawks' new $213 million basketball arena, Atlanta Journal & Constitution reported Friday.
The council approved the plan Thursday after eliminating a proposal calling for team owner Turner Broadcasting System Inc to drop an offer of free luxury boxes for politicians.
The council voted to consider the luxury box issue later, calling it a peripheral matter that could interfere with tight deadlines the project faces.
The revised deal was previously approved by the Atlanta-Fulton County recreation Authority but still must be approved by the Fulton County Commission.

The Hawks' have agreed to repay $140 million of tax-exempt bonds to be issued for arena construction. They originally pledged all of their revenues, including that from television and merchandising sales, to repay the bonds if ticket and concession sales were inadequate.

The team was forced to revise the agreement because National Basketball Association rules require that players and coaches be paid first. That would have reduced the amount of money the Hawks could pledge toward the bonds.
The new agreement pledges the team as collateral, so that if the Hawks default on the bonds, the team could be sold and the proceeds used to pay bond holders.
